recommendation_summary: Act now by keeping the shared folder for drafts only. On each release, a reviewer who is not the author places an unmodified copy in an archive that only reviewers can write. That reviewer's account and the approval time go on an append-only line, kept for seven years. The reply rejects typed initials and naming conventions as the approval record, and it also rejects a new document-management system. It proposes no optional additions. The one unmet item is the user's yes, since this changes the release step.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The signed customer contract requires every released document to keep its exact approved version, the approver's identity, and the approval time for seven years, and it requires that authors do not approve their own documents. You asked to keep the shared folder, add an APPROVED column of typed initials, and agree a naming convention for this week's delivery.
labels.Deleted: Typed initials and a naming convention as the approval record. A new document-management system.
labels.Bottleneck: Authors can still edit the shared folder, so an approval mark kept there can change after release.
labels.Checked myself: The contract terms, twelve remote authors, three reviewers, weekly releases, and the writable shared folder, as you described them.

note: The access-controlled reviewer archive with an append-only log ties non-author approval and approval time to an unmodified copy and keeps both for seven years.
